thread:
Cara (acme-corp): hey team — starting ~09:45 PST our embeddings throughput tanked. vectors/sec down ~6x vs yesterday. tokens/sec (text-gen) looks normal. no big change on our side except a client lib bump. example response shows dimension=1536 but our model expects 768. request id req_9f3a2c
Alice (support): thanks for filing — we're on it. can you confirm the model name & payload shape? any 4xx/5xx codes or 200s with wrong shape?
Cara (acme-corp): model: rdm-embed-compact-v1, sending batch of 32, each vector payload shape [[float... x 768]] — server replies still 200 but many results flagged as dim=1536 in app logs. no 5xx.
Alice (support): odd. please run with batch_size=1 and attach a single-request curl so we can reproduce.
Cara (acme-corp): fyi tried batch_size=1 — vectors/sec improves slightly but still ~2x lower than baseline. here's a minimal repro curl:

```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_acme_test" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rdm-embed-compact-v1","input":["hello world"]}'
```

Alice (support): got it. assigning to infra. @Bob can you check gpu queue and batcher telemetry? I see anomalous kvcache invalidation alerts from last deploy window.
Bob (ml-infra): looking. Cluster shows sustained GPU slot idle with CPU batcher backlog growing. grabbing logs for the batcher service now.
Bob (ml-infra): quick paste from batcher logs around 09:45:

```
[09:45:12] batcher INFO coalesce window=12ms, queued=120
[09:45:12] batcher WARN dim_mismatch_detected: incoming_dim=1536 expected=768, dropping_merge=True
[09:45:12] batcher ERROR kvcache_invalidate key=mdl-rdm-embed-compact-v1 scope=prefix
[09:45:13] gpu-scheduler WARN slot_util=22% backlog=86
```

Bob (ml-infra): looks like a batching heuristic change from today's runtime rollout allowed coalescing of variant requests even when dim mismatch detection was noisy. that triggered kvcache invalidation and caused many micro-batches that underutilized GPUs.
Dan (oncall): can we rollback the batching heuristic? runbook step 2 says to disable "aggressive-coalesce" flag. I'll trigger a controlled rollback for the pool serving rdm-embed-compact-v1.
Alice (support): sending Cara a quick mitigation: pin to rdm-embed-compact-v1:rev-42 (previous revision) and reduce client concurrency for a few minutes. Cara — instructions:

1) set header X-Model-Rev: rev-42
2) set batch_size=8
3) monitor vectors/sec and share new request ids

Cara (acme-corp): applying now. will report back.
Eileen (billing): checked account signals — no billing throttles or quota hits. some 429 bursts correlate with duplicated retries from the client after malformed responses; not a billing rule fault.
Cara (acme-corp): after pinning rev-42 and lowering batch size vectors/sec almost back to normal. pushing sample req id req_9f3a2c -> req_9f3a2c-2 shows expected dim=768 and latency stable. :thumbsup:
Dan (oncall): rollback completed for the runtime rollout at 09:58. watching gpu-slot-util — ramping to normal.
Bob (ml-infra): root cause summary: today's rollout changed coalescing so requests with intermittent embedding-dim header noise could be merged. that produced small micro-batches + kvcache invalidations for rdm-embed-compact-v1, leading to GPU underutilization and vectors/sec regression. fix: revert aggressive-coalesce flag + add stricter dim-consistency checks in batcher + metric: histogram of incoming embedding dims per model.
Alice (support): creating followup ticket and notifying release/rtx teams. Cara — leaving this thread open for 1hr to confirm stability. glad it's trending OK now. :white_check_mark:
Cara (acme-corp): thanks everyone — we'll monitor and let you know if it flares up. appreciated the fast turnaround.
deploy-bot: release rollback completed: rollout-id rl-2026-03-17-agg-coalesce -> reverted
Bob (ml-infra): postmortem action items: 1) revert shipped to stable, 2) add unit tests for dim-compat coalesce, 3) alert if dim histogram shows >1% off-expected dims for model, 4) add documentation for clients to not send stray dim headers.
Alice (support): closing SLA escalation after 1hr if stable. will re-open if Cara sees anything else.
